observed_original_abi.receiver_basis: placement, not a body read. The only reference to 0x00980510 in the entire program is one DATA word at 0x014440e4 = 0x014440d0 + 0x14, i.e. vtable slot +0x14 of the image based at 0x014440d0 (verified with a ReferenceManager sweep over the target: exactly one reference, of type DATA). A virtual slot implementation on this MSVC-compiled x86-32 binary receives the receiver in ECX. The body itself never reads ECX or any other register, so the two-instruction body is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall; the convention is a statement about how the slot is reached, not something the body can prove.
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: 0x00980510 is `MOV EAX,0x202`, a full 32-bit immediate write, so all four bytes of the result are defined (0x00000202) and nothing in the upper half is residual. That is what makes the type uint32 rather than bool or a narrow integer. Both the live Ghidra prototype (uint32_t UTFWin::PerspectiveEffect::GetProxyID(ILayoutElement * this)) and the abi_infer record (return_semantics integral_in_EAX, register_class integral) agree. The uncertainty is not the width but the NAME: 0x202 is an opaque per-class identifier, so the semantic type is a proxy id and uint32_t is the width the machine proves, not a claim about the ID space.
observed_original_abi.ghidra_parameter_note: Ghidra reports one parameter, `this`, at Stack[0x4]:4, typed ILayoutElement *. The reconstruction therefore declares the receiver in ECX and zero stack arguments, and treats the ILayoutElement spelling as decompiler-derived (no MSVC RTTI in this binary, per the project evidence note).

mechanics.shape: the entire body is one immediate store plus the terminator. There is no branch, no call, no memory operand, no arithmetic and no second path.
mechanics.constant: 0x202, written whole into EAX at 0x00980510. Decimal 514.
mechanics.receiver_dependence: none observable. ECX is never read; the value returned is the same for every receiver, which model test case test_receiver_independence exercises over six receivers including null, 0xffffffff and a stack address, and also asserts the receiver object's words are unchanged.
mechanics.memory_effects: none. The body writes no memory, so it cannot mutate the receiver or any global.
mechanics.globals: none. The listing names no data-segment address, and the body reaches memory nowhere.
mechanics.indirect_transfers: none. The body loads nothing through a pointer, so it performs no virtual dispatch of its own -- although it IS itself the target of a virtual dispatch (slot +0x14).
mechanics.direct_transfers: none. No CALL or JMP with an immediate operand exists in the body, so there is no statically-named callee. This is consistent with the briefing's empty callees and callers lists, which is a property of the code rather than a gap in the evidence.
mechanics.callers: none by direct call. The only reachability is the virtual dispatch through slot +0x14, whose call sites are data references and are therefore not enumerable as code callers.
mechanics.sibling_contrast: The other three GetProxyID bodies in this binary do real work: 0x0096fec0 (UTFWin::GlideEffect::GetProxyID) looks up a manager, allocates a 0x60-byte object tagged 'UTFWin/EA::UTFWinControls::FrameDrawable' and returns zero when the lookup fails; 0x0097e7d0 (UTFWin::ProportionalLayout::GetProxyID) calls 0x00920090 and then dispatches vtable slot +0x04 with a constant argument; 0x00836530 (UTFWin::VariableWidthDrawable::GetProxyID) is a scan over a table of 16-bit values. PerspectiveEffect's is the degenerate case: a class whose proxy id is fixed at compile time and needs no lookup.

return_semantics.basis: 0x00980510 writes EAX with a 32-bit immediate and 0x00980515 returns without touching EAX. No other instruction exists, so no path can alter the result.
return_semantics.ownership: pure. The body allocates nothing, acquires and releases nothing, and mutates no state. It is safe to call repeatedly on the same receiver and from any receiver state.

direct_transfers.note: the only control transfer in the body is the terminal RET at 0x00980515

unresolved_questions: The receiver convention is inferred, not observed. The body never reads ECX, so it is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall, and the persisted abi_infer record abstained for exactly that reason (verdict ABI_UNKNOWN). __thiscall here rests on the single fact that 0x00980510 is a vtable slot, plus the MSVC x86-32 convention that virtual members take the receiver in ECX. A direct (non-virtual) call to this address from somewhere outside the image would be indistinguishable in the body; no such call exists in this binary, so the risk is theoretical.

What 0x202 denotes. It is a per-class proxy identifier in an ID space this body never interprets, and the ID space is not recoverable from two instructions. The sibling implementations show the space is populated at runtime (0x0096fec0 allocates and tags objects with a class-name string; 0x0097e7d0 dispatches through a manager), which suggests 0x202 is an interned index assigned to UTFWin::PerspectiveEffect, but nothing here confirms that, its neighbours, or whether the space is dense.

The exact vtable extent. Slots +0x00..+0x5c are recorded and mutually consistent, but no null terminator appears in that window, and words observed at +0x60..+0x7c (0x010829f0, 0x00951230, 0x006f2f20) may belong to this image or to the next one. Nothing in this target's body depends on the answer.

Slot +0x18 (0x00980520) has no function record in Ghidra, so the slot immediately after GetProxyID is uncharacterised. It is the most likely place a related per-class override would sit, which makes it the obvious next target for this class.

The slots holding 0x00e31100, 0x00dde980 and 0x00b267f0 were not characterised. They are addresses above the low code range and are recorded as opaque words; whether they are code, data or imported thunks is unresolved here and does not affect this body.

The decompiler's `ILayoutElement *` parameter type is not independently confirmed. The binary carries no MSVC RTTI (per the project evidence note), so the base type comes from the imported Spore-ModAPI symbols. This record keeps the receiver opaque (struct PerspectiveEffect) rather than adopting the decompiler's base-class spelling, and flags the disagreement rather than resolving it.

Whether GetProxyID is genuinely virtual in the SDK's declaration or a non-virtual method that merely happens to occupy a slot cannot be checked here; the Spore-ModAPI headers are not present in this environment. The machine fact -- a slot at +0x14 -- is not in doubt either way.
